topics.title: C Tokens & Identifier Rules
topics.content:
Tokens are the smallest individual units in a program (32 keywords in C, Identifiers, Constants, Operators, Special Symbols, Strings)[cite: 1].
Identifier Rules:
- Must start with a letter or underscore (_).
- Can contain letters, digits, and underscores.
- Case-sensitive (e.g., sum ≠ Sum).
- Cannot be a keyword.

topics.title: Operators & Precedence
topics.content:
Operator Categories:
- Arithmetic (+, -, *, /, %)
- Relational (<, >, <=, >=, ==, !=)
- Logical (&&, ||, !)
- Assignment (=, +=, -=, *=, /=)
- Increment/Decrement (++, --)
- Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~, <<, >>)
- Conditional / Ternary (? :)
- Sizeof, Comma (,)

Pre vs Post Increment:
- Pre (++a): Increment first, then use.
- Post (a++): Use current value first, then increment.

Precedence Order (High to Low):
() → ++ -- → * / % → + - → < > <= >= → == != → && → || → = += -=

topics.title: Formatted and Unformatted I/O
topics.content:
Formatted I/O (Uses format specifiers):
- printf(), scanf()
- Format Specifiers: %d/%i (int), %f (float), %lf (double), %c (char), %s (string), %u (unsigned int), %ld (long int), %x (hex), %o (octal).

Unformatted I/O (No format specifiers):
- getchar(), putchar(), gets(), puts(), getch() (no echo), getche() (with echo).

topics.title: Control Statements & Looping
topics.content:
Control Statements:
- if-else, switch-case (expression must evaluate to int or char; float is not allowed).

Looping:
- for: Known iterations.
- while: Entry-controlled (may execute 0 times).
- do-while: Exit-controlled (executes at least once).
- Loop Control: break (exits loop immediately), continue (skips current iteration).

topics.title: User-Defined & Recursive Functions
topics.content:
Functions:
- Components: Declaration/Prototype, Definition, Call.
- Call by Value: Passes a copy; original variable remains unchanged.
- Call by Reference: Passes address (using pointers); changes affect the original variable.

Recursion:
- Function calling itself.
- Requires a Base Case (stopping condition) and a Recursive Case.

topics.title: Arrays & String Manipulations
topics.content:
Arrays:
- Collection of same data type elements in contiguous memory. Index starts at 0.
- Array name acts as a pointer to the first element (arr == &arr[0]).

Strings:
- Character array terminated by a null character ('\0').
- Key string.h Functions: strlen(), strcpy(), strcat(), strcmp() (returns 0 if equal), strrev(), strlwr(), strupr().

subsections.title: POINTERS, STRUCTURE AND DATA FILES IN C

topics.title: Pointers & Pointer Arithmetic
topics.content:
Pointers:
- Variable storing the memory address of another variable.
- Symbols: & (address-of), * (dereference / value at address).

Pointer Arithmetic:
- Incrementing (p++) moves pointer by sizeof(datatype) bytes.
- Valid: Pointer ± integer, Pointer - Pointer.
- Invalid: Pointer + Pointer, Pointer * integer.

topics.title: Structure vs Union
topics.content:
Structure (struct):
- Memory size equals the sum of all member sizes.
- Members have distinct memory locations; all can be accessed simultaneously.

Union (union):
- Memory size equals the size of the largest member.
- All members share the same memory location; only one can be accessed at a time.

topics.title: Pointers with Structures & Passing Mechanisms
topics.content:
Structure Pointers:
- Access members using the arrow operator (->), e.g., ptr->member equivalent to (*ptr).member.
- Can be passed to functions by value (copy) or by reference (pointer).

topics.title: File Operations & Access Methods
topics.content:
File Modes:
- 'r' (read), 'w' (write/overwrite), 'a' (append), 'r+' (read/write), 'wb'/'rb' (binary).

File I/O Functions:
- Character/String: fgetc(), fputc(), fgets(), fputs().
- Formatted: fprintf(), fscanf(). Block: fread(), fwrite().

Access Types:
- Sequential Access: Read/write linearly from start to end.
- Random Access: fseek(fp, offset, origin) with SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END; ftell(fp) returns current position; rewind(fp) resets to beginning.

subsections.title: C++ LANGUAGE CONSTRUCTS WITH OBJECTS AND CLASSES

topics.title: Namespaces, Functions & Default Arguments
topics.content:
Namespace: Container to prevent scope/name collisions (e.g., using namespace std).
Function Overloading: Same function name with different parameter types/counts (return type alone is insufficient).
Inline Functions: Suggests direct code insertion to reduce call overhead.
Default Arguments: Specified in function declarations; must be assigned from rightmost parameters leftward.

topics.title: Class, Objects & Access Specifiers
topics.content:
Classes & Access:
- Class: Template defining attributes and behaviors. Object: Instantiated variable of a class.
- Access Specifiers: private (default, accessible within class only), protected (accessible within class and derived classes), public (accessible everywhere).
- Outer Member Definitions: Scope resolution operator (::) used via ClassName::FunctionName().

topics.title: Constructors, Destructors & Memory
topics.content:
Life Cycle:
- Constructors: Special functions invoked automatically upon object instantiation (Default, Parameterized, Copy). No return type.
- Destructor (~ClassName): Invoked on object destruction; no arguments, cannot be overloaded.

Dynamic Memory:
- C++ uses new and delete / delete[] keywords.

topics.title: Static Members, Const, this & Friend Concepts
topics.content:
Key Concepts:
- this Pointer: Implicit pointer holding current object's address.
- Static Data Members: Single copy shared across all class objects. Static Functions can only access static members.
- Constant Objects/Functions: Const member functions promise not to alter object state.
- Friend Function/Class: Non-member entity granted explicit access to private and protected class members.

topics.title: Operator Overloading
topics.content:
Operator Overloading:
- Redefines standard operators for user-defined types.
- Post-increment overload uses a dummy int parameter: operator++(int).
- Non-overloadable operators: . (member access), .* (pointer-to-member), :: (scope resolution), ?: (ternary), sizeof.

topics.title: Data Conversion & Inheritance Types
topics.content:
Data Conversion:
- Basic to Class: Handled via Constructors.
- Class to Basic: Handled via Casting Operators (operator type()).

Inheritance:
- Deriving new classes from base classes.
- Access Effects: Public inheritance keeps public/protected levels; Protected turns public into protected; Private turns all into private.
- Hierarchy Types: Single, Multiple, Multilevel, Hierarchical, Hybrid, Multipath (Diamond problem resolved using virtual base class).

topics.title: Constructors & Destructors in Inheritance
topics.content:
Execution Order:
- Constructors execute top-down: Base Class → Derived Class.
- Destructors execute bottom-up: Derived Class → Base Class.

subsections.title: PURE VIRTUAL FUNCTION AND FILE HANDLING

topics.title: Virtual Functions & Abstract Classes
topics.content:
Polymorphism:
- Virtual Functions: Overridden in derived classes for dynamic (runtime) binding using vtables.
- Pure Virtual Function: Function declared with = 0 and no implementation.
- Abstract Class: Class containing at least one pure virtual function; cannot be instantiated directly.

topics.title: C++ File Handling & Stream Formatting
topics.content:
Streams & Formatting:
- Stream Classes (<fstream>): ifstream (reading), ofstream (writing), fstream (both).
- File Modes: ios::in, ios::out, ios::app, ios::ate, ios::trunc, ios::binary.
- Formatting & Manipulators (<iomanip>): setw(n), setprecision(n), setfill(c), endl.

topics.title: Templates & Standard Template Library (STL)
topics.content:
Templates:
- Generic programming using template <typename T> for functions and classes.

Standard Template Library (STL):
- Containers: vector (dynamic array), list, deque, stack, queue, set, map.
- Iterators: Pointer-like objects used for container traversal.
- Algorithms: Pre-defined functions like sort(), reverse(), find().

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.content:
Mechanism:
- Keywords: try (encloses risky code), throw (raises exception), catch (handles exception).
- Catch All: catch(...) catches any unhandled exception type.
- Rethrow: An empty throw; inside a catch block rethrows current exception.
- Exception Specification: Modern C++ uses noexcept to signify non-throwing functions.

questions.question: How many keywords are there in C language?
questions.explanation: Standard C language defines 32 reserved keywords.

questions.question: What is the output of: int a = 5; printf("%d", a++);
questions.explanation: a++ is post-increment, so it uses the current value (5) for printing and then increments to 6.

questions.question: What is the output of: int a = 5; printf("%d", ++a);
questions.explanation: ++a is pre-increment, so it increments a to 6 first and then prints it.

questions.question: Which format specifier is used for double?
questions.explanation: %lf is used for double, %f for float, %d for integer, and %ld for long integer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an unformatted I/O function?
questions.explanation: getchar() reads a single character without needing format specifiers.

questions.question: Which loop executes at least once even if the condition is false?
questions.explanation: do-while is an exit-controlled loop that evaluates its condition after executing the body once.

questions.question: In 'Call by Value', the original argument value is:
questions.explanation: Call by Value passes a copy of the argument, so modifications inside the function do not alter the original variable.

questions.question: A function calling itself is known as:
questions.explanation: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself directly or indirectly.

questions.question: Array indexing in C starts from:
questions.explanation: C arrays are zero-indexed; the first element is at index 0.

questions.question: Which string library function returns the length of a string?
questions.explanation: strlen() returns the count of characters up to, but not including, the null terminator.

questions.question: What is the null character in C strings?
questions.explanation: The null character '\0' (ASCII 0) marks the end of a string in C.

questions.question: strcmp() returns 0 when:
questions.explanation: strcmp returns 0 if both strings match character for character.

questions.question: A pointer variable stores:
questions.explanation: A pointer is a variable designed specifically to hold memory addresses.

questions.question: If int *p, then *p represents:
questions.explanation: * is the dereference operator, returning the value stored at the memory location held in p.

questions.question: Which operator is used to obtain the address of a variable?
questions.explanation: & is the address-of operator in C/C++.

questions.question: If int arr[5], then the expression 'arr' is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: An array name decays into a pointer to its first element (&arr[0]).

questions.question: The array access expression arr[i] is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: In pointer arithmetic, arr[i] translates directly to *(arr + i).

questions.question: The total memory allocated for a union is:
questions.explanation: Because all members share memory, a union's size equals that of its largest member.

questions.question: The memory size allocated for a structure is equal to:
questions.explanation: Structures assign separate memory space for each member (excluding padding).

questions.question: The arrow operator (->) is used when accessing members via a:
questions.explanation: ptr->member is short for (*ptr).member when working with structure pointers.

questions.question: Which file mode opens a file for writing and creates a new file if it does not exist?
questions.explanation: "w" mode creates a new file or overwrites an existing file for writing.

questions.question: The fseek() function is used for:
questions.explanation: fseek() moves the file position indicator to a specified location, enabling random file access.

questions.question: Which function resets the file position pointer to the beginning of the file?
questions.explanation: rewind(fp) sets the file position to the start, equivalent to fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET).

questions.question: In fseek(), SEEK_END refers to:
questions.explanation: SEEK_END measures offset relative to the end of the file.

questions.question: The default access specifier for members of a C++ class is:
questions.explanation: In C++ classes, members are private by default (whereas struct members are public by default).

questions.question: Which C++ feature allows multiple functions with the same name but different parameter lists?
questions.explanation: Function overloading allows identical function names differentiated by signatures.

questions.question: A constructor function always shares the same name as:
questions.explanation: Constructors must have the exact same name as the class.

questions.question: A constructor is automatically executed when:
questions.explanation: Constructors run automatically at the point of object instantiation.

questions.question: A destructor is automatically executed when:
questions.explanation: Destructors execute automatically when an object's lifetime ends.

questions.question: A destructor's name begins with which symbol?
questions.explanation: Destructors are named ~ClassName().

questions.question: Which keyword is used for dynamic memory allocation in C++?
questions.explanation: C++ uses 'new' for allocation and 'delete' for deallocation.

questions.question: The implicit 'this' pointer points to:
questions.explanation: 'this' is an implicit pointer holding the memory address of the invoking object.

questions.question: A static data member is shared by:
questions.explanation: Only one copy of a static member exists, shared across all instances of a class.

questions.question: A friend function of a class can access:
questions.explanation: Friend functions have access to all private, protected, and public class members.

questions.question: Which statement about a friend function is correct?
options: It is a member of the class
It is not a member of the class
questions.explanation: A friend function is declared within a class scope but is not a member of that class.

questions.question: Default arguments in C++ functions must be declared starting from:
questions.explanation: Default parameters must be placed from right to left in the parameter list.

questions.question: Which operator CANNOT be overloaded in C++?
questions.explanation: Scope resolution (::), member access (.), pointer-to-member (.*), ternary (?:), and sizeof cannot be overloaded.

questions.question: To overload the post-increment operator (a++), the function signature uses:
questions.explanation: Post-increment overloading requires a dummy integer argument: operator++(int).

questions.question: Conversion from a basic data type to a class type is performed using a:
questions.explanation: A constructor accepting a basic type argument handles basic-to-class type conversion.

questions.question: Conversion from a class type to a basic data type is performed using a:
questions.explanation: An overloaded conversion/casting operator function converts a class object into a primitive type.

questions.question: In single inheritance, constructor execution order is:
questions.explanation: Constructors execute from base class to derived class.

questions.question: In inheritance, destructor execution order is:
questions.explanation: Destructors execute in reverse order: derived class first, then base class.

questions.question: The diamond (multipath) problem occurs in which type of inheritance?
questions.explanation: It occurs when a derived class inherits from multiple intermediate classes that share a common base.

questions.question: The diamond problem is resolved using:
questions.explanation: Virtual base classes ensure only one copy of the grandparent base class is inherited.

questions.question: When class B inherits from class A:
options: A is derived, B is base
B is derived, A is base
questions.explanation: Class A is the base (parent) class, and class B is the derived (child) class.

questions.question: Virtual functions enable which type of binding?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions support runtime/dynamic binding through virtual function tables (vtables).

questions.question: A pure virtual function is declared as:
questions.explanation: Pure virtual functions end with '= 0;' and carry no body definition in the base class.

questions.question: A class containing at least one pure virtual function is an:
questions.explanation: Any class with at least one pure virtual function becomes an abstract class.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding abstract classes?
questions.explanation: Objects of an abstract class cannot be instantiated directly.

questions.question: Which C++ stream class is used for reading files?
questions.explanation: ifstream handles input file stream operations (reading).

questions.question: Opening a file in ios::app mode ensures that operations:
questions.explanation: ios::app automatically moves output write position to the end of the file.

questions.question: Which stream manipulator sets the minimum field width for output?
questions.explanation: setw(n) configures output width to n characters.

questions.question: Which header file is required to use parameterized I/O manipulators like setw?
questions.explanation: <iomanip> defines stream manipulators with arguments.

questions.question: Templates in C++ facilitate:
questions.explanation: Templates allow generic functions and classes to work across varying data types.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to introduce a template definition?
questions.explanation: The 'template' keyword starts template declarations (e.g., template <typename T>).

questions.question: STL stands for:
questions.explanation: STL stands for Standard Template Library.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an STL container?
questions.explanation: printf is an I/O function from C, not an STL container.

questions.question: The 'vector' container in STL represents a:
questions.explanation: vector is a contiguous dynamic array capable of resizing automatically.

questions.question: The primary role of an Iterator in STL is to:
questions.explanation: Iterators function similarly to pointers, traversing elements inside STL containers.

questions.question: Which set of keywords is used for C++ exception handling?
questions.explanation: try, throw, and catch form the exception handling construct in C++.

questions.question: The 'throw' keyword is used to:
questions.explanation: throw explicitly signals/raises an exception condition.

questions.question: The handler statement catch(...) will catch:
questions.explanation: Ellipsis inside catch (...) acts as a fallback catching any thrown data type.

questions.question: To rethrow an exception from inside a catch block, use:
questions.explanation: An empty 'throw;' expression inside a catch block rethrows the exception being handled.

questions.question: Marking a function with the 'noexcept' specifier guarantees that:
questions.explanation: noexcept informs the compiler that the function promises not to throw any exceptions.

questions.question: What is sizeof(char) in standard C?
questions.explanation: sizeof(char) is defined by the C standard to be exactly 1 byte.

questions.question: In standard C, main() function returns:
questions.explanation: The standard signature for main() returns an int status code to the operating system.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid identifier name?
questions.explanation: Identifiers cannot begin with a numeric digit.

questions.question: What is printed by printf("Hello\0World"); ?
questions.explanation: The '\0' acts as a string terminator, causing output to stop right after 'Hello'.

questions.question: What is the output of printf("%d", sizeof(10.5)); on standard systems?
questions.explanation: Floating point literal 10.5 defaults to type double, which occupies 8 bytes.

questions.question: Encapsulation refers to:
options: Hiding data and binding it with methods
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data members and methods into a single unit while restricting direct external access.

questions.question: The literal meaning of Polymorphism is:
questions.explanation: Polymorphism derives from Greek, meaning 'many forms' (same interface, different behavior).

questions.question: Under protected inheritance, public members of the base class become:
questions.explanation: Protected inheritance converts public base members to protected visibility in the derived class.

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding constructor return types?
options: Has no return type at all
questions.explanation: Constructors do not specify any return type, not even void.

questions.question: A copy constructor parameter must be passed as a:
questions.explanation: Copy constructors take arguments by reference (e.g., ClassName(const ClassName &obj)) to avoid infinite recursion.

questions.question: Which pointer assignment expression is valid?
questions.explanation: Pointers can only store addresses of lvalues/variables, not literals or rvalue expressions.
